_comment: How the song is laid under each cut. Times are seconds in the trailer (out) and in the song (src). rate < 1 slows the record and drops its pitch (asetrate), lp / hp are a low-pass / high-pass in Hz, vib is tape wow depth (0..1), mono folds it to one channel, room is a small room around it (wet, 0..1), gain is linear. mute windows silence the whole mix (the hard cut before the scare); muteFloor (dBFS) leaves the tape's own hiss under them at that level instead of digital silence. duck lowers the song to gain under every voice line (a cue from assets/audio/vo), ramping over ramp seconds, so a line reads over it; the landscape cut has no voice lines, so there it does nothing. Times may be numbers or strings in the landscape cut's marks (TURN, DROP, DURATION, ACT2 = DROP-TURN; trailer.js) so the plan moves with them.

landscape._comment: The song plays straight from the first frame to the last, at its own speed and pitch, with nothing done to it. The only break is the hard cut to silence at the drop, before the face.

portrait._comment: The song comes in on the first daylight shot, warps through the TV, cuts out when the set switches off, and comes back slower from beyond the door until the latch shuts it out. After that: tape hiss before the scare, a dropout as the camera hits the floor, and the record again, faint, under the title. Mono and in a small room throughout, as the camcorder's mic would hear it. loudness (LUFS) and truePeak (dBTP) are the targets the finished mix is mastered to, the levels Shorts, Reels and TikTok play at.
